loading-button: harness: first-render / first.noEntryAnimation false: mountFrames minOp is 1 and mountTopRange is 0, so nothing fades or moves. The check fails only because it needs absolute |dy| < 0.5. In the ports the label sits at a static -0.5px from the button centre (rm.xfade.toSuccess.startDy -0.5, resting endDy about -0.45) because of font metrics. The script should compare how much dy changes across mount frames (max minus min for each part) instead of absolute dy.

baseline: label-crossfade in.startOp, in.opAt33, in.opAt67 and out.opAt67 (for example toSuccess.in.startOp 0.176 vs 0, toIdle.in.opAt33 0.494 vs at most 0.45): motion-v starts the fade in the same frame the node mounts, so the first sampled frame is already about one frame into the fade. Because opAt33 and opAt67 are read relative to that first frame, the whole curve shifts by under one frame. durMs (127, 117, 122) and the curve shape are inside the baseline. A 0.03 ratio tolerance equals about 3ms on this slope. Read times from the trigger (or extrapolate to where opacity is 0) and allow one frame (about 17ms), or compare the time to reach opacity 0.5 as an ms check.

baseline: success-subscribe / subscribe.check.fracAt70 0.381 vs at most 0.378: the same frame-phase effect (startFrac 0.018). drawMs is 250, inside tolerance. The 0.03 tolerance on a fixed-time sample is under 6ms.

harness: first-render / first.noEntryAnimation false: minOp 1 and topRange 0. This is the same static -0.5px text dy offset as the other ports. Compare the change in dy across mount frames, not absolute dy.

harness: tab-order / tab.success.back 'button:Subscribed Subscribed' vs 'button:SubscribedSubscribed': the label is built from raw textContent, and the space is template whitespace between the visible label and the sr-only live span. harness: keyboard-activate: kbd.enter.apply.{busy, ariaDisabled, busyEndMs, resultText, clickCount} are missing, with scriptError 'no click event #0 on button 2'.
